title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 145 (Auditor to sign audit reports, etc.)

content.overview: The person appointed as an auditor of the company shall sign the auditor's report or sign or certify any other document of the company required by law to be signed or certified by the auditor, and the qualifications, observations or comments on financial transactions or matters which have any adverse effect on the functioning of the company mentioned in the auditor's report shall be read before the company in general meeting and shall be open to inspection by any member of the company. Those qualifications, observations or comments shall be stated in thick type or in italics.
content.glance: The auditor must sign the report; adverse qualifications, observations or comments are read at the general meeting, open to inspection, and printed in thick type or italics.
content.study:
## Section 145 — Auditor to sign audit reports

**Signature.** The appointed auditor signs the auditor's report (and any other document required by law to be signed or certified by the auditor), in accordance with section 141(2) for firm appointments.

**Adverse matter.** Qualifications, observations or comments on financial transactions or matters which have any adverse effect on the functioning of the company must be:
- read before the company in general meeting;
- open to inspection by any member; and
- stated in thick type or in italics.

Signing is the formal act; content duties of the auditor are in section 143.

This note is a focused study aid; the topic remains under source and current-law review.

hypotheticals.question: Must every observation in the audit report be read at the general meeting?
hypotheticals.analysis: Section 145 requires reading of qualifications, observations or comments that have any adverse effect on the functioning of the company. Not every observation necessarily falls in that category.
